task.description:
WF-03 Step 4 gate (hard gate on TEST-DESIGNER) for ISS-0119. Derive your verdict from the TEST CODE ITSELF, not from TEST-DESIGNER's result.summary or from the spec's prose. The spec (test/specs/ISS-0119.md) is evidence to be checked, not testimony to be accepted.

WHAT IS BEING GATED: test/docs/requirement_status_invariants_test.exs (A0-A8 with A4 split into A4a/A4b, plus two negative-control blocks), test/support/status_history.ex (the path-parameterised helper), and test/specs/ISS-0119.md (the spec carrying the fail-first evidence). TEST-DESIGNER reports 13 passed, zero warnings, format clean.

BACKGROUND YOU NEED. A4 went red on its FIRST EVER run against three previously unknown malformed entries in frozen volume 1 (4803 REQ-053 missing note:, 4896 REQ-056 timestamp: instead of at: at line 4899, 5050 REQ-054 missing note:). That drove a design amendment (§13) which CODE-DESIGN-VALIDATOR FAILED once -- because a declared record could cite the CURRENT volume, making the exception list a declare-to-silence mechanism -- then passed once the closed-and-pinned rule was added. So this test file now carries the project's first mechanical enforcement of the append-only rule, and the specific way it could be worthless is by asserting less than it appears to.

THE FOUR CHECKS THAT MATTER MOST -- do these first and do them by reading code:

1. DO THE NEGATIVE CONTROLS DRIVE THE SAME FUNCTION A4b ASSERTS ON? This is the single most important check in this gate. TEST-DESIGNER states both negative controls call the same `a4b_findings/1` that the A4b block asserts on. IF THEY INSTEAD CALL A PARALLEL REIMPLEMENTATION -- a second copy of the logic written inside the test, or a differently-parameterised path that skips the real code path -- THEN THEY PROVE NOTHING ABOUT A4b and the 'A4b bites' claim collapses. Read both blocks and the function they call. Confirm identity of the code path, not merely similarity of the output.

2. IS THE CLOSED-AND-PINNED RULE GENUINELY INDEPENDENT OF SET EQUALITY? §13.5 requires it fire independently and EVEN WHEN the cited violation genuinely exists on disk. TEST-DESIGNER's negative control 2 claims exactly that shape: set equality reports 0 and 0, and A4b still goes red on `records citing a volume that is not closed-and-pinned (1) ... volume status: "current" (must be "closed")`. VERIFY THAT IS WHAT THE CODE ACTUALLY DOES -- that `not_closed_and_pinned` is computed independently of `undeclared`/`unfound`, and that a green set-equality cannot suppress it. TEST-DESIGNER also discloses a deliberate structural choice you must rule on: A4b is ONE block with ONE assert over five independently computed lists, on the reasoning that separate asserts would let ExUnit's first-failure abort hide the closed-and-pinned result behind a set-equality failure -- the masking §13.5 forbids. Judge whether that reasoning holds and whether it satisfies C3 (one test block per assertion), given C3's own rationale was precisely to stop first-failure abort from hiding a later assertion.

3. WAS ANYTHING UNDER docs/status/ EDITED TO MAKE A TEST GREEN? This is the gate-integrity check and the one core-directives.md forbids absolutely. ORCH has already established the branch-level numbers for you to check against: `git diff --numstat main...HEAD -- docs/status/` returns 165/0 for the index, 140/0 for v2, and 38/0 for volume 1 -- ALL INSERTIONS, ZERO DELETIONS on every one. Confirm volume 1's 38 are the EOF closure footer only and that lines 1-5,766 are untouched; confirm the index's three known_shape_anomalies records match the on-disk entries rather than having been trimmed to whatever the detector happened to emit; and confirm TEST-DESIGNER's fixtures live under a temp dir with on_exit cleanup and never write to the real files.

4. IS COVERAGE COMPLETE AGAINST ISS-0119's ACTUAL ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA? Read docs/issues/ISS-0119.yaml. Its two remedies were (a) make the file readable again, bounded, with full history preserved and nothing dropped, and (b) a header that prescribes an EXECUTABLE safeguard, with the req: SCOPE-CHANGE convention stated explicitly. Map each to a runnable assertion or state plainly that it is unasserted. Where something genuinely cannot be mechanically asserted (prose being executable, for instance), say so rather than stretching an assertion to cover it -- an overclaimed mapping is worse than an acknowledged gap.

ALSO CHECK: no test is skipped, tagged-out, or deferred; fixtures are isolated and self-sufficient; nothing hardcodes the index location (the helper is meant to be path-parameterised, which is what makes the pre-fix run possible); the fail-first evidence in the spec still stands given §13 changed A4 (A3 is the assertion the fail-first proof rests on, and TEST-DESIGNER states A0/A1/A2/A3/A3b/A6/A7 are unchanged -- verify A3 specifically, since if it changed, the pre-fix demonstration recorded in the spec no longer describes the code on the branch); and the spec does not restate REVIEWER's expired no-added-failure proof.

RUN THE TEST FILE YOURSELF -- `mix test test/docs/requirement_status_invariants_test.exs` -- and quote the real result. Do not run the full suite; TEST-RUNNER owns that at Step 4c.

Do not edit any file other than your own handoff. On FAIL, name each gap with its specific missing element.
acceptance_criteria: The verdict is derived from the test code itself, and result.summary names what was read
Check 1 confirms by reading code whether both negative controls drive the SAME function A4b asserts on, or a parallel reimplementation
Check 2 confirms the closed-and-pinned rule is computed independently of set equality and cannot be suppressed by a green set comparison, and rules on whether the single-assert structure satisfies C3
Check 3 confirms nothing under docs/status/ was edited to make a test pass -- volume 1 lines 1-5,766 untouched, index records matching on-disk entries, fixtures confined to a temp dir with cleanup
Every ISS-0119 remedy is mapped to a runnable assertion or explicitly declared unasserted, with no overclaimed mappings
A3 is specifically verified unchanged, so the spec's fail-first evidence still describes the code on the branch
No test is skipped, tagged-out or deferred, and fixtures are isolated and self-sufficient
mix test on the invariant file was run by the validator and its real output quoted
No file other than this handoff was modified

result.summary:
PASS. Verdict re-derived from the code, not from TEST-DESIGNER's summary. Read in full: test/docs/requirement_status_invariants_test.exs (739 lines, all 13 blocks plus every private helper), test/support/status_history.ex (522 lines), test/specs/ISS-0119.md (sections 1-7), docs/issues/ISS-0119.yaml, docs/status/requirement_status.index.yaml (volumes:, known_anomalies:, known_shape_anomalies:), the v2 header, the volume-1 append diff, and the on-disk entries at volume-1 lines 4801-4806 / 4894-4901 / 5048-5054. Ran `mix test test/docs/requirement_status_invariants_test.exs` myself: "Running ExUnit with seed: 874457, max_cases: 32 / ............. / Finished in 1.8 seconds (1.8s async, 0.00s sync) / Result: 13 passed" -- 13 blocks, 0 failures, 0 warnings. `mix format --check-formatted` on both files is clean.

CHECK 1 -- NEGATIVE CONTROLS DRIVE THE REAL FUNCTION. CONFIRMED BY IDENTITY, not similarity. The A4b block (lines 159-163) is `findings = a4b_findings(@index_path); assert a4b_clean?(findings), a4b_message(@index_path, findings)`. Negative control 1 (line 196) and negative control 2 (line 236) each call `a4b_findings(Path.join(dir, "index.yaml"))`, `a4b_clean?/1` and `a4b_message/2` -- the same three private functions, defined once each at lines 447, 467 and 560. There is no second copy of the logic anywhere in the file: exactly one `defp a4b_findings` definition exists. The only difference between the A4b block and the controls is the index path argument, which is the whole point of the path-parameterisation. `a4b_findings/1` in turn delegates to the real Letflow.Test.StatusHistory (`parse_index/1`, `shape_anomalies/1`, `entries/1`); it does not re-derive shape violations inside the test. The 'A4b bites' claim stands.

CHECK 2 -- CLOSED-AND-PINNED IS INDEPENDENT, AND C3 IS SATISFIED. `a4b_findings/1` builds a five-key map whose `not_closed_and_pinned:` is `Enum.reject(declared, &closed_and_pinned?(volumes, &1))` -- a function of `declared` and `volumes` only. It never reads `undeclared`/`unfound`, and there is no short-circuit or guard between them. `a4b_clean?/1` is `Enum.all?` over all five keys, so a green set comparison cannot suppress it; a non-empty `not_closed_and_pinned` alone makes the assert fail. Negative control 2 proves this at runtime and its fixture has exactly the shape section 13.5 demands: v2's entry genuinely has no `note:` on disk AND the declared record matches it exactly, so the test first asserts `{findings.undeclared, findings.unfound} == {[], []}` (set equality green), then `refute a4b_clean?(findings)`, then `[%{path: _, entry_line: 3}] = findings.not_closed_and_pinned`, and finally that the rendered message carries both `records citing a volume that is not closed-and-pinned` and `volume status: "current"`. That is the declare-to-silence hole the design gate FAILed section 13's first version on, and it is now mechanically closed.

C3 RULING: the single-assert structure PASSES. C3's rationale was that ExUnit's first-failure abort must not hide a later assertion. Five separate asserts in one block would reintroduce exactly that. The chosen structure does the opposite: `a4b_message/2` renders all five categories unconditionally, each with its own count and its own labelled line-per-record block (`(none)` when empty), so a set-equality failure and a closed-and-pinned failure appear together in one output. Literal C3 compliance holds too -- one `test` block, one `assert`. Nothing is masked; C3's purpose is served better here than by a split.

CHECK 3 -- NO GATE WAS SATISFIED BY EDITING WHAT IT MEASURES. `git diff --numstat main...HEAD -- docs/status/` reproduces 165/0, 140/0, 38/0 -- zero deletions on all three. Volume 1's diff is a single hunk `@@ -5764,3 +5764,41 @@`: the three context lines are unchanged and all 38 additions are the EOF closure footer (VOLUME 1 -- CLOSED marker, targeted-read instructions, successor pointer, known-anomaly note). Lines 1-5,766 are untouched, which A6 also pins by SHA-256. Index records match disk rather than being trimmed to the detector: line 4803 REQ-053 started has req/event/agent/at and no note; 4896 REQ-056 started carries `timestamp: "2026-08-19T02:40:35Z"` at line 4899 exactly as `found_line: 4899` claims; 5050 REQ-054 started has no note. All three carry `should_have_been:`/`cause:` beyond what the detector emits, i.e. richer than the minimum, not trimmed to it. Volume 1's 182 `- req:` entries match the index's `entries: 182`. Fixtures are confined to `Path.join(System.tmp_dir!(), "iss0119-<name>-<unique_integer>")` with `on_exit(fn -> File.rm_rf!(dir) end)`; `write_volume!/2` and `write_index!/3` are only ever called with that dir, and nothing under docs/status/ is written by any block.

CHECK 4 -- COVERAGE AGAINST ISS-0119, WITH THE GAPS NAMED RATHER THAN STRETCHED. Remedy (a) 'make it readable again, bounded, full history preserved, nothing dropped' is fully mechanised: bounded = A3 (resolves the current volume through `current_volume/2` and takes ceilings from the index, hardcoding neither) with A3b as an honestly-labelled calibration guard; nothing dropped = A6 (SHA-256 over volume 1's frozen 5,766-line prefix -- byte-level preservation, the strongest form of 'nothing dropped'), A5 (vocabulary set equality in BOTH directions, so a silent normalisation fails), A4b (shape set equality in both directions); history reachable = A1 (bidirectional index/disk), A2 (exactly one current), A7 (closure footer names the successor). Remedy (b) 'a header prescribing an EXECUTABLE safeguard, with req: SCOPE-CHANGE stated explicitly' is PARTIALLY mechanised, and I am stating the boundary rather than overclaiming: A8 asserts the current volume's header contains the literal tokens for all six events plus `REQ-NNN` and `SCOPE-CHANGE`, both ceiling restatements rebuilt from the index (so no unchecked prose copy of the numbers exists), and `known_shape_anomalies:`. A8 asserts TOKEN PRESENCE. It does NOT and cannot assert that the header's HOW-TO-APPEND procedure is actually executable -- that the two shell one-liners run, that step 5's `git diff --numstat` check is followed, or that the `req: ISS-NNNN is not legal` prose is understood. Prose being executable is not mechanically assertable by a unit test; I read the v2 header directly (steps 1-6, both shells, the five-field entry shape, the two-value `req:` list with the ISS-NNNN prohibition) and confirm it satisfies remedy (b) on inspection, but I am recording it as ASSERTED ONLY AT TOKEN LEVEL. Equally unasserted: the TASK_QUEUE.md:133 correction that caused the three SCOPE-CHANGE anomalies -- A4a asserts the DATA, never the INSTRUCTION. Both are acknowledged gaps, not covered ones.

A3 SPECIFICALLY VERIFIED UNCHANGED. Extracted the A3 block from 6443eb2 (pre-section-13) and from HEAD and diffed them: IDENTICAL, byte for byte, 35 lines. A0 likewise IDENTICAL. A3 still sits at line 105 with its assert at line 122 -- the exact line numbers the spec's pre-fix failure output quotes (`requirement_status_invariants_test.exs:105`, stacktrace `:122`), so the recorded fail-first demonstration still describes the code on this branch. The helper diff 6443eb2..HEAD adds functions only (`shape_anomalies/1`, `entry_shape_anomalies/2`, `pair_misnamed/3`, `shape_record/6`, `field_line/2`, `denull/1`); no existing `def`/`defp` was removed or resignatured, and `current_volume/2`, `within_bounds?/3`, `measure/1`, `default_ceilings/0` -- everything A3 and A0 traverse -- are untouched.

REMAINING CHECKS. No `@tag :skip`, no `@moduletag`, no TODO, no deferred or commented-out block anywhere in the test file, the helper, or the spec -- all 13 blocks are runnable and all 13 ran. Fixtures are self-sufficient: each control creates its own dir, its own volumes and its own index, and depends on no other test having run; `async: true` is safe because `System.unique_integer([:positive])` makes each dir distinct. No hardcoded secret or connection string. The helper hardcodes no index location -- its only path literal is `"requirement_status.yaml"` joined onto the caller-supplied `status_dir` inside the documented `{:no_index_fallback, _}` branch, which is precisely the mechanism that makes the pre-fix run possible. The spec does NOT restate REVIEWER's expired no-added-failure proof: section 7 declares it EXPIRED in bold and routes the baseline to TEST-RUNNER at Step 4c, and section 5 states plainly that the section-13 rework did not re-run the pre-fix worktree.

issues.description: Remedy (b) of ISS-0119 is asserted at token level only. A8 checks that the current volume's header CONTAINS `SCOPE-CHANGE`, the six event names, `REQ-NNN`, `known_shape_anomalies:` and both ceiling restatements -- it cannot assert that the HOW-TO-APPEND procedure is executable, that the two shell one-liners run, or that the `req: ISS-NNNN is not legal` prose is present as guidance. I read the v2 header and it does satisfy remedy (b) on inspection; recording the boundary so no later run mistakes A8 for a proof of executability. Not a gate failure -- prose executability is not mechanically assertable by a unit test.

The instruction defect that produced the three `event: SCOPE-CHANGE` anomalies (TASK_QUEUE.md:133 stating the convention in the wrong field) is corrected on this branch as a doc edit with no assertion behind it. A4a asserts the DATA is free of new vocabulary drift; nothing asserts the INSTRUCTION stays corrected, so a future edit could reintroduce the wrong-field convention and A4a would only notice after entries were written under it. Acknowledged gap, not a blocker -- A4a is the second line of defence and it does fire.

`a4b_key/1` keys a record on {path, entry_line, kind, field, found_as} and deliberately excludes `found_line`, so a declared record could carry a wrong `found_line` and still satisfy set equality. Materially covered today: the only record with a `found_line` is the volume-1 `misnamed_field`/`at` one, and `unparseable_at/2`'s from_declared limb reads that exact line and would fail if it did not hold a parseable ISO-8601 value (verified on disk: line 4899 is `timestamp: "2026-08-19T02:40:35Z"`). Worth noting for a future `misnamed_field` on a non-`at` field, where no limb would re-check `found_line`.

The index declares `entries:` per volume (182 for volume 1, 0 for volume 2) and no assertion compares it to `length(SH.entries(path))`. Harmless for volume 1 because A6's digest pins the bytes, and I verified the count matches on disk (182 `- req:` lines); it would become load-bearing if a future closed volume's declared count drifted. Suggested as a one-line addition to A1 or A6 in a later run, not a gate condition here.

result.next_action: Proceed to Step 4c (TEST-RUNNER). TEST-RUNNER must re-establish the main-vs-branch baseline independently -- REVIEWER's Step 3d no-added-failure proof is expired and the spec correctly declines to restate it, and REVIEWER noted the project gate is currently RED for pre-existing ISS-0109/ISS-0116-class reasons unrelated to this branch. The four MINOR issues above are observations for a follow-up run; none blocks Step 4c.
